canonical_work.title: Hindi to Mundari Translation Dataset Corpus
canonical_work.verified_provider_description: Public provider repository describes a corpus of 17,826 Hindi-to-Mundari sentence pairs created through collaboration between Microsoft Research India, Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, and Karya.

identity_and_deduplication.canonicalization_rule: README, LICENSE, COPYRIGHT, TSV and provider/project descriptions are manifestations/components of one dataset release and must not be counted as independent corroborating sources.
identity_and_deduplication.relationship_to_muntts: Related project ecosystem, but not identical to the Mundari TTS corpus; do not merge translation-pair counts with audio-recording counts.

not_supported_without_additional_evidenc: claim that every sentence is independently elicited cultural testimony
scope.cultural_scope_rule: Individual sentence pairs must not be promoted as cultural propositions without item-level provenance, contextual support and governance review.

rights_access_consent.provider_license_statement: Provider describes the dataset as released under the non-commercial version of the Karya Public License; LICENSE.txt and COPYRIGHT.txt are part of the repository.
rights_access_consent.consent_inference: No participant consent, identity, locality or permission beyond the provider's published release terms is inferred from public availability.
required_before_reuse: inspect exact LICENSE.txt and COPYRIGHT.txt terms
hash ingested file if lawful and necessary

promotion.reason: Dataset identity, provider-reported size and file name are verified, but row-level exact locators, manifestation hash, provenance and complete reuse conditions were not established in this run.

gaps: exact provider commit/release manifestation not frozen in MLHKP
TSV row count and schema not independently validated in this run
row-level source/provenance and translation-review metadata not established
complete downstream reuse implications require LICENSE/COPYRIGHT review
no sentence-level cultural claim may be inferred solely from corpus membership
